newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy total bank lending growth slows in March - ABI.
newsitem.headline: Italy total bank lending growth slows in March - ABI.

text.p: The rate of growth in total Italian bank lending slowed in March but foreign currency loans showed an increase, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said.

Total loans extended by banks holding short-term deposits, accounting for all high street banks, rose 3.03 percent year-on-year in March to 888.0 trillion lire after a 3.63 percent increase in February, ABI's latest monthly report said.
Lire loans grew by only 3.05 percent in March to 802.0 trillion lire after a rise of 3.78 percent registered in February year-on-year.

However, foreign currency loans increased by 2.77 percent to 86.0 trillion lire in March after a 2.25 percent rise in February, marking a clear improvement for the first time in several months, the ABI report said.

ABI said the trend of commercial bank lending in March was to be seen in a "scenario where signs of an improvement in the economic climate are coming only from expectations of a rise in industrial orders over the coming months."
But given that the current overall economic environment was so far little changed, dynamism in the bank financing sector was therefore rather limited, ABI said.
